relevance_note: Case report of a woman with a heterozygous TNFAIP3 variant and two affected children: "A novel heterozygous variant was identified in TNFAIP3; ENST00000237289 c.1906C>T".
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; the paper has no data tables (Table S1 is a supplementary population-genetics table not included in the Markdown). A Python script in the scratch directory only assembled the JSON from values and spans typed in by hand, then checked that every span occurs verbatim in the paper and every row has every schema field. Individuals: the proband (index case), her two children (labelled by the paper's phrase 'a girl of age 4 years' and 'a boy aged 6 and a half'), the proband's father (clinical history only; the paper does not say he was genetically tested, so he has no variant row), and three previously published individuals summarised in the Discussion, each with source_reference_in_review (refs 16, 15 and 8). The ref-15 case has no variant row because the text gives no variant; the ref-16 and ref-8 rows record only the generic genotype text. The groups mentioned without individual detail (the 22 Japanese cases, ref 6; Zhou et al. cohort, ref 4; Aeschlimann et al., ref 14) and the 7 CAPS comparison patients were not given rows. Children's variant rows rest on 'investigated for autosomal dominant inheritance' plus 'Genetic analysis of family members found segregation with the inflammatory clinical phenotypes'; the paper never states their genotype or zygosity in words, so zygosity and inheritance are 'not reported' (rule 8), and functional assays (done on the proband's cells only) are not copied to them. Children's disease label left 'not reported' although the Discussion calls 'the younger sibling we presented here' one of the HA20 'cases'. Proband age at diagnosis records the clinical AOSD diagnosis at age 21; the age at genetic diagnosis is not given. Variant notes: the authors first thought c.1906C>T was missense, then describe it as an exonic splice variant at the terminal residue of exon 7 ('n.1972 Cgt/Tgt') producing 'c.1906 Cat/TAG, p.His636fsTer1' and deletion of exon 8; the transcript printed is the Ensembl ID ENST00000237289 (no NM_ accession); rs200138929 printed with the GRCh37 coordinate. Functional assays were done while the proband was on tocilizumab, which the authors say could have interfered. Checklist: ANA, RF and ACPA negative are recorded as excluded features, but 'autoantibodies (ANA/other)' stays 'not reported' because other autoantibodies are not addressed (narrow vs broad rule). No within-paper contradictions about any person's features were found; minor inconsistency: the abstract says 'patients’ sera' (plural) while the text describes one patient's serum.

functional_evidence_statement.value: Proband cDNA (PBMCs) showed a mutant allele with deletion of exon 8; Western blot confirmed loss of transcript by nonsense-mediated decay resulting in A20 haploinsufficiency; after LPS a greater percentage of patient monocytes became p65 positive than in healthy controls (not statistically significant); IL-1β and IL-18 production significantly increased in patient PBMC after LPS and ATP; serum ASC specks significantly higher than the healthy control range.
span: The patient’s cDNA produced a mutant allele containing deletion of exon 8 (Figure 1B).
Loss of transcript by nonsense-mediated decay resulting in A20 haploinsufficiency was confirmed by Western blot (Figure 1C).
Following stimulation, greater percentage of patient monocytes became p65 positive compared with monocytes from healthy controls. However, this did not reach a statistical significance (Figure 2).

The production of IL-1β and IL-18 was found to be significantly increased in the patient’s PBMC compared with healthy controls after stimulation by priming and activation with LPS and ATP, respectively (Figures 3A,B).
We found that patient serum contained significantly higher numbers of ASC specks compared with our healthy control range (Figure 3I).
